description.narrative:
Strengthening Community Participation through Engagement (SCOPE) is what HANDLE seeks to use as a strategy to address incidences ofvulnerability caused by the effects of Covid – 19 such as trauma, and mental illness among women, and people living with disabilityin Nwoya District. In this strategy, SCOPE will apply Interpersonal Psychotherapy for Groups (IPT-G) to give psychosocial support (treat) to women, and persons with different abilities that have been assessed and identified to be having depressive symptoms (or depression) as a result of different traumatic experiences triggered by factors such as covid-19, to regain their meaningful active participation in decision making and other community engagement activities. In this innovation, the vulnerable persons are first screened for depression/trauma using standard tools, and those with low and moderate depression are put into groups of 8-12 members. A trained facilitator/promoter (village health team) will conduct meetings with the group(s) once or twice in a week for sessions for aperiod of 12 -15 weeks (3 months), in which the women open up on the causes of their depression and how they have been handling before solutions to the different problems are generated within the group, and this will be facilitated by a trained promoters (Villagehealth team). The group will ensure all information and discussions remain confidential and only for group consumption alone. Midterm and post IPT assessment is done to track progress in the treatment process. After 12 weeks, the groups are integrated into livelihoods economic activities through Village Saving and Loan Association for group sustainability as they continue sharing and interacting alongside performing economic activities. As it is in most communities in Northern Uganda; women, children, youths and Persons living with disabilities are the most vulnerable groups and are at high risk of suffering from exploitation , abuse and/violence withvery limited or no involvement in community issues, whichlargely results in depression. World over, it has been noted that depression impairs functionality and leads to isolation of victims from actively participating in meaningful activities at different levels (Helena Verdeli et al). Depression, if not treated, may lead to mental meltdown and might result in attempts to terminate life or certainly death. According to Theodore D. Wachs et al, depressive orders are a common source of disability among women in addition to the economic and human costs of maternaldepression.
In most rural communities, many people are not aware of depression, its causes and the effects. This partly explains why such groups rarely or totally do not register their participation in community activities including but not limited todecision making processes. Through this innovation, we want to see the mental ability of the vulnerable persons regained and their participation in productive activities strengthened, level of vulnerability amongst women of reproductiveage and people with disability reduced, and service delivery improved in Community.

participating-org.narrative: HOPE ALERT NETWORK FOR DEVT AND LOC

The purpose of having Hope Alert Network for Development and Local Empowerment operating was to create space for women and youth indecision making and improving livelihood stand of the entire community, and fulfilment of children’s rights, in particulartheir right to healthy and psychosocial development. From the time the organization was founded, its major work has been mainly on youth livelihoods, gender equality advocacy and education, and women empowerment. HANDLE is a member of Men Engage Gender quality network in Uganda advocating for gender equality among men and women.
It may be recalled that from 1986 to 2008 Northern Uganda was engulfed ina brutal conflict between LRA and government of Uganda. Thousands of people were displaced in the several IDPs across the sub region. Youth, children and women experienced the most gruesome abuses. While the conflict continuously drifted to Central African Republic, the situation of youth and women in Northern Uganda Region was aggravated by a sombre interest shown by government and other development agencies whose response to the needs of youth and women remained pronounced in advocacy, Education and mobilization of resources. Real expenditures during implementation hardly reflected the said interest. In 2008 youth stakeholders’ meeting to discuss the findings was held in Gulu supported by HRDP. The meeting reflected on some of the findings and recommendations to provide sustainable development and this has then resulted to the formation of Hope Alert Network for Development and Local Empowerment (HANDLE) Uganda in 2009 by some youth activists and registered under National NGO in 2012.
In the past three years, HANDLE under its GBV project worked with 24 women caucuses and leaders and built their capacities in decision-making and policy influence, including lobbying for women’s issues. Key achievements includes election of 8 women leaders into positions of influence at the local council level and in newly created sub counties where they were able to make meaningful decisions; enactment of 12 bylaws on women’s issues including girls education, alcoholism, child protection and domestic violence; influencing budgetary allocation for women-led projects that resulted in to improved service delivery in Nwoya District. 90 Role model men were identified and trained as champion of change to other men in the fight against Gender based violence and formed in to VSLA groups where they were supported with business start-up capital to sustain their livelihoods and that of their families.
INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE The Vision: World where no child knows poverty, vulnerable individuals are economically empowered.
Mission Statement: We seek to achieve our mission through commitment to the delivery of programs thatensures measurable quality of work and lasting impact for the people we serve.
Mission: Commitment for the delivery of programs that ensure measurable quality of work and lasting impact for the people we serve
HANDLE works with the community and accountable to its project stakeholders who includes the government technical offices and the political leaders both at local and national level. Some of the key roles played by these stakeholders includes and not limited to; coordination, mobilization,andtechnical advices to the project.
However some of the areas that makes HANDLE a unique organization includes: Community approach; HANDLE uses a community – based model where the vulnerable persons are empowered to know their rights through building their capacity. This has seen most of them gain advocacy strengths and skills which helped them in application even after the project ends.
Multidisciplinary: HANDLE is recognised for its defence of women’s’ rights at local and national levels. HANDLE has the developed programs in diverse areas such as health, land rights, economic empowerment, human rights, gender equality and livelihoods aligned with the aspirations and rights of vulnerable communities that at the core of its intervention.
Solid anddedicated team: the team’s technicalknow–how is recognized in the defence of gender equality and women’s rights participation in life of society, the defence of human rights and the rights related to reproductive health, in particular. Its success canbeexplained by its ability to involve and listento rights–holders and its desire to empower them in the medium and long term.
Strong anchorage with local and international community: HANDLE has over the last ten years worked in partnership with community-based structures including 64 VSLA groups, 90 role model men, community activists, human right defenders, community based facilitators, cultural and religious leaders.
